docs.title: Ariadne
docs.text:
Ariadne is a Python toolkit to harmonize source vocabularies into the OHDSI Standardized Vocabularies.

It currently supports three workflows:

  • Conditions: exact matching and hierarchy matching (for identifying a parent concept when no exact standard match is available).
  • Drugs: prepares source codes for inserting into the OHDSI Boiler software as described here.
  • Procedures: exact source-to-standard concept mapping for procedure vocabularies.

The toolkit is designed to be extensible, allowing for the addition of new workflows (e.g., measurements, devices) and mapping strategies as needed.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Clean-up: normalizes source terms per mapping rules, removing non-essential information.
  • Verbatim term mapping: maps terms that (almost) exactly match standard concepts using normalization (lowercasing, punctuation removal, stemming).
  • Embedding vector search: retrieves semantically similar standard concepts as mapping candidates.
  • LLM-assisted exact mapping: selects the best standard concept from candidates.
  • Hierarchy matching (Conditions): finds parent concepts for unmatched terms in the standard hierarchy.
  • Evaluation: compares outputs against gold-standard mappings.

def evaluate_concept_search(
    search_results: pd.DataFrame,
    output_file: str | Path,
    gold_standard_file: str = "data/gold_standards/exact_matching_gs.csv",
    source_id_column: str = "source_concept_code",
    term_column: str = "cleaned_term",
    matched_concept_id_column: str = "matched_concept_id",
    matched_concept_name_column: str = "matched_concept_name",
    match_rank_column: str = "match_rank",
) -> None:
    """
    Evaluate the concept search results against the gold standard.

    Args:
        search_results: Pandas DataFrame containing the results of the concept search.
        output_file: Path to save the evaluation results.
        gold_standard_file: Path to the CSV file containing the gold standard mappings.
        source_id_column: Name of the column in the search results with source concept IDs.
        term_column: Name of the column in the search results with the search terms.
        matched_concept_id_column: Name of the column in the search results with matched concept IDs.
        matched_concept_name_column: Name of the column in the search results with matched concept names.
        match_rank_column: Name of the column in the search results with the rank of the matched concepts.

    Returns:
        None. Execution results are written to the specified output file.
    """
    detail_strings = []
    gold_standard = pd.read_csv(resolve_path(gold_standard_file))
    evaluated_gs_count = 0
    mean_average_precision = 0
    recall_1 = 0
    recall_3 = 0
    recall_10 = 0
    recall_25 = 0

    grouped = search_results.groupby(source_id_column)
    for source_id, group in grouped:
        gs_entry = gold_standard[gold_standard[SOURCE_ID] == source_id]
        if gs_entry.empty:
            continue
        gs_entry = gs_entry.iloc[0]
        gs_source_term = gs_entry[SOURCE_TERM]
        gs_concept_id = gs_entry[TARGET_CONCEPT_ID]
        gs_concept_id_b = gs_entry[TARGET_CONCEPT_ID_B]
        gold_predicate = gs_entry[PREDICATE]
        gold_predicate_b = gs_entry[PREDICATE_B]
        if gold_predicate == BROAD_MATCH:
            gs_concept_id = None
        if gold_predicate_b == BROAD_MATCH:
            gs_concept_id_b = None
        if gs_concept_id is None and (gs_concept_id_b is None or math.isnan(gs_concept_id_b)):
            continue
        evaluated_gs_count = evaluated_gs_count + 1
        gs_rank = group.loc[group[matched_concept_id_column] == gs_concept_id, match_rank_column]
        if gs_concept_id_b is not None:
            gs_rank_b = group.loc[group[matched_concept_id_column] == gs_concept_id_b, match_rank_column]
            if not gs_rank_b.empty:
                if gs_rank.empty or gs_rank_b.iloc[0] < gs_rank.iloc[0]:
                    gs_rank = gs_rank_b
                    gs_concept_id = gs_concept_id_b
        detail_strings.append(f"Source term: {gs_source_term} ({source_id})")
        detail_strings.append(f"Searched term: {group[term_column].iloc[0]}")
        if gs_rank.empty:
            detail_strings.append("Gold standard concept not found")
            gs_concept_name = gs_entry[TARGET_CONCEPT_NAME]
            detail_strings.append(f"Correct target was: {gs_concept_name} ({gs_concept_id})")
        else:
            gs_rank = gs_rank.iloc[0]
            detail_strings.append(f"Gold standard concept rank: {gs_rank}")
            mean_average_precision = mean_average_precision + 1 / gs_rank
            if gs_rank <= 1:
                recall_1 = recall_1 + 1
            if gs_rank <= 3:
                recall_3 = recall_3 + 1
            if gs_rank <= 10:
                recall_10 = recall_10 + 1
            if gs_rank <= 25:
                recall_25 = recall_25 + 1

        detail_strings.append("")

        table = group[[match_rank_column, matched_concept_id_column, matched_concept_name_column]].copy()
        correct = np.where(table[matched_concept_id_column] == gs_concept_id, "Yes", "")
        if gs_concept_id_b:
            correct_b = np.where(table[matched_concept_id_column] == gs_concept_id_b, "Yes", "")
            correct = np.where(correct == "Yes", "Yes", correct_b)

        table.insert(1, "Correct", correct)
        detail_strings.append(table.to_string(index=False))
        detail_strings.append("")

    mean_average_precision = mean_average_precision / evaluated_gs_count
    recall_1 = recall_1 / evaluated_gs_count
    recall_3 = recall_3 / evaluated_gs_count
    recall_10 = recall_10 / evaluated_gs_count
    recall_25 = recall_25 / evaluated_gs_count

    summary_strings = [
        f"Evaluated gold standard concepts: {evaluated_gs_count}",
        f"Mean Average Precision: {mean_average_precision}",
        f"Recall@1: {recall_1}",
        f"Recall@3: {recall_3}",
        f"Recall@10: {recall_10}",
        f"Recall@25: {recall_25}",
    ]

    with open(output_file, "w", encoding="UTF-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(summary_strings))
        f.write("\n\n")
        f.write("\n".join(detail_strings))
        f.write("\n")

    print(f"Evaluation complete. Results written to {output_file}")

def evaluate(
    selection_results: pd.DataFrame,
    gold_standard_file: [str|Path] = "data/gold_standards/exact_matching_gs.csv",
    source_id_column: str = "source_concept_code",
    term_column: str = "cleaned_term",
    mapped_concept_id_column: str = "mapped_concept_id",
    mapped_concept_name_column: str = "mapped_concept_name",
    mapped_rationale_column: Optional[str] = "mapped_rationale",
    mapped_method_column: Optional[str] = "map_method",
    source_ids: Optional[List[str]] = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Evaluate the concept selection results against the gold standard.

    Args:
        selection_results: Pandas DataFrame containing the results of selection results.
        gold_standard_file: Path to the CSV file containing the gold standard mappings.
        source_id_column: Name of the column with source concept IDs.
        term_column: Name of the column with source terms.
        mapped_concept_id_column: Name of the column with mapped concept IDs.
        mapped_concept_name_column: Name of the column with mapped concept names.
        mapped_method_column: Optional: Name of the column with mapping methods, e.g. "verbatim" or "llm".
        mapped_rationale_column: Optional: Name of the column with mapping rationales.
        source_ids: Optional list of source concept IDs to evaluate. If None, evaluate all.

    Returns:
        A Pandas DataFrame with the evaluation results.
    """
    gold_standard = pd.read_csv(resolve_path(gold_standard_file),
                                dtype={SOURCE_ID: str})

    if mapped_method_column:
        output_mapped_method_column = mapped_method_column
    else:
        output_mapped_method_column = "map_method"

    selection_results.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)
    evaluation_results = []
    for index, row in selection_results.iterrows():
        source_id = str(row[source_id_column])
        if source_ids is not None and source_id not in source_ids:
            continue

        gold_entry = gold_standard[gold_standard[SOURCE_ID] == source_id]
        if gold_entry.empty:
            continue
        gold_entry = gold_entry.iloc[0]
        gold_target_concept_id = gold_entry[TARGET_CONCEPT_ID]
        gold_target_concept_id_b = gold_entry[TARGET_CONCEPT_ID_B]
        gold_predicate = gold_entry[PREDICATE]
        gold_predicate_b = gold_entry[PREDICATE_B]

        mapped_concept_id = int(row[mapped_concept_id_column])
        if mapped_method_column and mapped_method_column in row:
            map_method = row[mapped_method_column]
        else:
            map_method = "unknown"
        is_correct = (
            (mapped_concept_id == gold_target_concept_id and gold_predicate == EXACT_MATCH)
            or (mapped_concept_id == gold_target_concept_id_b and gold_predicate_b == EXACT_MATCH)
            or (mapped_concept_id == -1 and gold_predicate == BROAD_MATCH)
            or (mapped_concept_id == -1 and gold_predicate_b == BROAD_MATCH)
        )
        result_row = {
            SOURCE_ID: source_id,
            SOURCE_TERM: gold_entry.get(SOURCE_TERM),
            output_mapped_method_column: map_method,
            TARGET_CONCEPT_ID: gold_target_concept_id,
            TARGET_CONCEPT_NAME: gold_entry.get(TARGET_CONCEPT_NAME),
            PREDICATE: gold_predicate,
            TARGET_CONCEPT_ID_B: gold_target_concept_id_b,
            TARGET_CONCEPT_NAME_B: gold_entry.get(TARGET_CONCEPT_NAME_B),
            PREDICATE_B: gold_predicate_b,
        }
        if term_column != SOURCE_TERM:
            result_row[term_column] = row[term_column]
        result_row.update(
            {
                mapped_concept_id_column: mapped_concept_id,
                mapped_concept_name_column: row[mapped_concept_name_column],
                "is_correct": is_correct,
            }
        )
        if mapped_rationale_column and mapped_rationale_column in row:
            result_row[mapped_rationale_column] = row[mapped_rationale_column]

        evaluation_results.append(result_row)
    evaluation_df = pd.DataFrame(evaluation_results)

    # Add overall accuracy as a column:
    accuracy = evaluation_df["is_correct"].mean()
    evaluation_df["overall_accuracy"] = accuracy

    return evaluation_df

Public API

docs.title: build_prediction_rows(results, hierarchy_settings)
docs.text:
Extract prediction rows from pipeline results for evaluation.

Handles regular attributes (single dict, list of dicts) and paired interprets_interpretation structures via :func:split_interprets_pairs. Each row carries relationship_groups: the SNOMED role group number(s) of the attribute value, ;-separated (a value shared by several groups appears once).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default results list[dict]

Pipeline result dicts from process_hierarchy.

required hierarchy_settings HierarchySettings

Pipeline configuration. hierarchy.attributes gives each attribute key's OHDSI relationship (attribute_category). When hierarchy.mrcm.grouping is configured, results without role_groups (e.g. cached before grouping existed) are grouped on the fly; otherwise their relationship_groups is None.

required

Returns:

Type Description list[dict]

List of flat dicts ready for pd.DataFrame.

def build_prediction_rows(results: list[dict], hierarchy_settings: HierarchySettings) -> list[dict]:
    """Extract prediction rows from pipeline results for evaluation.

    Handles regular attributes (single dict, list of dicts) and paired
    ``interprets_interpretation`` structures via :func:`split_interprets_pairs`.
    Each row carries ``relationship_groups``: the SNOMED role group number(s) of the
    attribute value, ``;``-separated (a value shared by several groups appears once).

    Args:
        results: Pipeline result dicts from ``process_hierarchy``.
        hierarchy_settings: Pipeline configuration. ``hierarchy.attributes`` gives each attribute
            key's OHDSI relationship (``attribute_category``). When ``hierarchy.mrcm.grouping`` is
            configured, results without ``role_groups`` (e.g. cached before grouping existed) are
            grouped on the fly; otherwise their ``relationship_groups`` is ``None``.

    Returns:
        List of flat dicts ready for ``pd.DataFrame``.
    """
    relationship_for = hierarchy_settings.relationship_by_attribute()
    mrcm_settings = hierarchy_settings.mrcm

    def _category(attr_key: str, default: str) -> str:
        return relationship_for.get(EXTRACTION_KEY_ALIASES.get(attr_key, attr_key), default)

    pred_rows: list[dict] = []
    for result in results:
        source_meta = {
            "source_key": result.get("source_key"),
            "source_concept_id": result.get("source_concept_id"),
            "source_concept_code": result.get("source_concept_code"),
            "source_vocabulary_id": result.get("source_vocabulary_id"),
            "source_term": result.get("source_term"),
        }
        if "attributes" not in result:
            continue
        role_groups = result.get("role_groups")
        if role_groups is None and mrcm_settings.grouping.enabled:
            role_groups = group_attributes(
                result["attributes"], mrcm_settings, result.get("llm_role_groups")
            ).role_groups
        group_lookup = _role_group_lookup(role_groups)

        def _groups(key: str, concept: dict) -> str | None:
            return group_lookup.get((key, str(concept.get("concept_id"))))
        for attr_key, attr_value in result["attributes"].items():
            if attr_value is None:
                continue

            # Handle paired interprets_interpretation tuples
            if attr_key == "interprets_interpretation":
                if not isinstance(attr_value, list):
                    attr_value = [attr_value]
                for sub_key, concept in split_interprets_pairs(attr_value):
                    if isinstance(concept, dict):
                        pred_rows.append({
                            **source_meta,
                            "predicted_target_concept_id": concept.get("concept_id"),
                            "predicted_target_concept_name": concept.get("concept_name"),
                            "predicted_target_concept_code": concept.get("concept_code"),
                            "attribute_category": _category(sub_key, f"Has {sub_key}"),
                            "relationship_groups": _groups(sub_key, concept),
                        })
                continue

            attr_type = _category(attr_key, attr_key)
            # Handle list of concept dicts (new multi-value format)
            if isinstance(attr_value, list):
                for item in attr_value:
                    if item and isinstance(item, dict):
                        pred_rows.append({
                            **source_meta,
                            "predicted_target_concept_id": item.get("concept_id"),
                            "predicted_target_concept_name": item.get("concept_name"),
                            "predicted_target_concept_code": item.get("concept_code"),
                            "attribute_category": attr_type,
                            "relationship_groups": _groups(attr_key, item),
                        })
            # Handle single concept dict
            elif isinstance(attr_value, dict):
                pred_rows.append({
                    **source_meta,
                    "predicted_target_concept_id": attr_value.get("concept_id"),
                    "predicted_target_concept_name": attr_value.get("concept_name"),
                    "predicted_target_concept_code": attr_value.get("concept_code"),
                    "attribute_category": attr_type,
                    "relationship_groups": _groups(attr_key, attr_value),
                })
    return pred_rows

def evaluate_results(
    results: list[dict],
    gs_path: str,
    output_dir: Path,
    hierarchy_settings: HierarchySettings,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Produce a combined evaluation table (full outer join of GS and predictions).

    Columns:
        source_key, source_concept_id, source_concept_code, source_vocabulary_id,
        source_term, attribute_category,
        gs_target_concept_id, gs_target_concept_code, gs_target_concept_name,
        predicted_target_concept_id, predicted_target_concept_code, predicted_target_concept_name,
        matched, status (``match`` / ``missed`` / ``extra``).

    Summary statistics are printed and the combined table is saved to CSV.

    Args:
        results: List of pipeline result dicts from ``process_hierarchy``.
        gs_path: Path to the gold-standard CSV.
        output_dir: Path wherhe the output CSV should be saved.
        hierarchy_settings: Pipeline configuration (see :func:`build_prediction_rows`).

    Returns:
        Combined evaluation DataFrame.
    """
    # --- build predicted rows ---
    pred_rows = build_prediction_rows(results, hierarchy_settings)
    pred_df = pd.DataFrame(pred_rows)
    source_cols = ["source_key", "source_concept_id", "source_concept_code",
                   "source_vocabulary_id", "source_term"]
    if pred_df.empty:
        pred_df = pd.DataFrame(columns=source_cols + [
            "predicted_target_concept_id", "predicted_target_concept_name",
            "predicted_target_concept_code", "attribute_category", "relationship_groups"])

    # --- load gold standard ---
    gs_df = pd.read_csv(gs_path)
    gs_df = gs_df.rename(columns={
        'target_concept_id': 'gs_target_concept_id',
        'target_concept_code': 'gs_target_concept_code',
        'target_concept_name': 'gs_target_concept_name',
    })

    # --- composite source key + numeric target join key ---
    for df in (gs_df, pred_df):
        df['source_key'] = (
            df['source_vocabulary_id'].astype(str) + ':' + df['source_concept_code'].astype(str)
        )
    gs_df['_join_target'] = pd.to_numeric(gs_df['gs_target_concept_id'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
    pred_df['_join_target'] = pd.to_numeric(pred_df['predicted_target_concept_id'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    combined = gs_df.merge(
        pred_df,
        on=['source_key', '_join_target', 'attribute_category'],
        how='outer',
        suffixes=('_gs', '_pred'),
    )

    # Reconcile source descriptor columns from both sides (GS wins, pred fills gaps)
    for col in ('source_concept_id', 'source_concept_code', 'source_vocabulary_id', 'source_term'):
        gs_col, pred_col = f'{col}_gs', f'{col}_pred'
        if gs_col in combined.columns:
            combined[col] = combined[gs_col].fillna(combined[pred_col])
            combined.drop(columns=[gs_col, pred_col], inplace=True)

    combined.drop(columns=['_join_target'], inplace=True)

    # --- flags ---
    has_gs = combined['gs_target_concept_id'].notna()
    has_pred = combined['predicted_target_concept_id'].notna()
    combined['matched'] = has_gs & has_pred
    combined['status'] = 'match'
    combined.loc[has_gs & ~has_pred, 'status'] = 'missed'
    combined.loc[~has_gs & has_pred, 'status'] = 'extra'

    # --- order columns nicely ---
    leading = ['source_key', 'source_concept_id', 'source_concept_code',
               'source_vocabulary_id', 'source_term', 'attribute_category',
               'gs_target_concept_id', 'gs_target_concept_code', 'gs_target_concept_name',
               'predicted_target_concept_id', 'predicted_target_concept_code', 'predicted_target_concept_name',
               'matched', 'status']
    extra_cols = [c for c in combined.columns if c not in leading]
    combined = combined[[c for c in leading if c in combined.columns] + extra_cols]

    # Sort for readability
    combined = combined.sort_values(['source_key', 'attribute_category', 'status']).reset_index(drop=True)

    # --- summary stats ---
    n_gs = int(has_gs.sum())
    n_pred = int(has_pred.sum())
    n_match = int(combined['matched'].sum())
    precision = n_match / n_pred * 100 if n_pred else 0.0
    recall = n_match / n_gs * 100 if n_gs else 0.0
    f1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) if (precision + recall) else 0.0

    logger.info("Gold standard rows: %d", n_gs)
    logger.info("Predicted rows:     %d", n_pred)
    logger.info("Matched:            %d", n_match)
    logger.info("Precision:          %.1f%%", precision)
    logger.info("Recall:             %.1f%%", recall)
    logger.info("F1:                 %.1f%%", f1)

    # --- save ---
    out_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "hierarchy_attribute_evaluation.csv")
    combined.to_csv(out_path, index=False)
    logger.info("Combined evaluation saved: %s (%d rows)", out_path, len(combined))
    return combined

docs.title: stated_parent_evaluator
docs.text:
Evaluate selected stated parents against the proximal primitive parents of held-out SNOMED concepts.

For a held-out concept the reference is its proximal primitive parent set: the most specific primitive ancestors (within the allowed parent set) in the inferred hierarchy. Outcomes:

  • exact: the selected parents equal the reference set.
  • partial: at least one reference parent selected; every other selected parent is an ancestor of a reference parent.
  • too_general: every selected parent is a proper ancestor of a reference parent. The classifier places the concept too high but not in the wrong branch.
  • wrong: at least one selected parent is not an ancestor-or-self of any reference parent, so the classifier can place the concept in the wrong branch.
  • no_reference: the source has no primitive ancestor in the allowed set (e.g. a situation) or no OMOP concept_id.

Source code in src/ariadne/evaluation/stated_parent_evaluator.py 
def classify_parents(predicted: set[int], expected: set[int], ancestry: PrimitiveAncestry) -> str:
    """Classify a selected parent set against the reference proximal primitive parents."""
    if not expected:
        return "no_reference"
    if predicted == expected:
        return "exact"

    def covers(parent_id: int) -> bool:
        return any(parent_id == e or ancestry.is_ancestor(parent_id, e) for e in expected)

    if not all(covers(p) for p in predicted):
        return "wrong"
    return "partial" if predicted & expected else "too_general"

def evaluate_stated_parents(
    details: pd.DataFrame,
    conn: psycopg.Connection,
    schema: str,
    settings: ParentSelectionConfig,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compare ``build_stated_parents_map`` details with the held-out concepts' proximal primitive parents.

    Returns:
        One row per source with selected and reference parents and the outcome.
    """
    selected = details.groupby("source_concept_id", sort=False).agg(
        source_term=("source_term", "first"),
        parent_ids=("parent_concept_id", lambda s: set(int(v) for v in s)),
        parent_names=("parent_concept_name", lambda s: "; ".join(s)),
    )
    source_ids = [cid for key in selected.index if (cid := _concept_id(key)) is not None]
    ancestry = fetch_primitive_ancestry(source_ids, conn, schema, settings)

    rows = []
    for key, row in selected.iterrows():
        cid = _concept_id(key)
        expected = proximal_primitive_parents(cid, ancestry) if cid is not None else []
        rows.append(
            {
                "source_concept_id": key,
                "source_term": row["source_term"],
                "selected_parents": row["parent_names"],
                "reference_parents": "; ".join(c.concept_name for c in expected),
                "outcome": classify_parents(row["parent_ids"], {c.concept_id for c in expected}, ancestry),
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def build_attribute_table(
    hierarchy_settings: HierarchySettings,
    if_exists: Literal["append", "skip", "rebuild"] = "append"
) -> None:
    """Build the pgvector SNOMED attribute table from OMOP relationships.

    Args:
        hierarchy_settings: Hierarchy settings containing ``index_build`` defaults.
        if_exists: Behavior when target tables already contain rows:
            - ``"append"``: insert without truncating.
            - ``"skip"``: skip populated tables.
            - ``"rebuild"``: truncate first, then insert.
    """
    if if_exists not in {"append", "skip", "rebuild"}:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported if_exists mode: {if_exists}")

    embedding_cache_dir = Path(hierarchy_settings.index_build.embedding_cache_folder)
    rebuild = if_exists == "rebuild"

    embedding_cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if if_exists == "skip":
        conn = _pg_connect()
        try:
            if check_populated(conn, "snomed_attribute"):
                logger.info("snomed_attribute already populated — skipping.")
                return
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # Build embeddings first (with parquet checkpoints), then create/upload tables.
    df_attr = load_attributes_from_db(hierarchy_settings.snomed_relationships)
    batch_files, dim = _prepare_attribute_embedding_batches(
        df_attr,
        embedding_batch_size=hierarchy_settings.index_build.embedding_batch_size,
        embedding_cache_dir=embedding_cache_dir,
    )
    if dim is None:
        probe = get_embedding_vectors(["probe"])
        dim = int(probe["embeddings"].shape[1])
    logger.info("Embedding dimension: %d", dim)

    conn = _pg_connect()
    try:
        create_table(conn, dim=dim)

        conn = insert_attributes(
            conn,
            batch_files,
            upload_batch_size=hierarchy_settings.index_build.embedding_batch_size,
            rebuild=rebuild,
        )

        create_embedding_index(conn)
    finally:
        conn.close()

    logger.info("Index build complete.")

def check_populated(conn: psycopg.Connection, table: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if *table* already contains at least one row.

    Args:
        conn: psycopg connection (read access is enough).
        table: Table name to check.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if the table is non-empty.
    """
    schema = get_environment_variable("VOCAB_SCHEMA")
    table_path = f"{schema}.{table}"
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT to_regclass(%s)", (table_path,))
        if cur.fetchone()[0] is None:
            return False
        cur.execute(
            sql.SQL("SELECT 1 FROM {schema}.{table} LIMIT 1").format(
                schema=sql.Identifier(schema),
                table=sql.Identifier(table),
            )
        )
        return cur.fetchone() is not None

def create_table(conn: psycopg.Connection, dim: int) -> None:
    """Create ``snomed_attribute`` table.

    Safe to call when tables already exist (uses ``CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS``).

                id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,

                concept_code       VARCHAR(255)  NOT NULL,

                embedding          halfvec({dim})

def insert_attributes(
    conn: psycopg.Connection,
    batch_files: list[Path],
    upload_batch_size: int,
    rebuild: bool = False,
) -> psycopg.Connection:
    """Insert pre-embedded parquet batches into ``snomed_attribute``.

    Args:
        conn: Admin psycopg connection (returned — may be replaced on retry).
        batch_files: Parquet files containing pre-embedded attribute rows.
        upload_batch_size: Number of rows per INSERT chunk.
        rebuild: When True, truncate the table first.

    Returns:
        The (possibly reconnected) psycopg connection.
    """
    schema = get_environment_variable("VOCAB_SCHEMA")
    if rebuild:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                sql.SQL("TRUNCATE TABLE {schema}.snomed_attribute RESTART IDENTITY")
                .format(schema=sql.Identifier(schema))
            )
        conn.commit()
        logger.info("Truncated snomed_attribute.")

    total_rows = 0
    insert_sql = sql.SQL(
        "INSERT INTO {schema}.snomed_attribute "
        "(concept_id, concept_code, concept_name, attribute_category, embedding) "
        "VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s)"
    ).format(schema=sql.Identifier(schema))

    for file_index, batch_file in enumerate(batch_files, start=1):
        df_batch = pd.read_parquet(batch_file)
        rows = [
            (int(r["concept_id"]), str(r["concept_code"]), str(r["concept_name"]),
             str(r["attribute_category"]), list(r["embedding"]))
            for _, r in df_batch.iterrows()
        ]
        total_rows += len(rows)

        for i in range(0, len(rows), upload_batch_size):
            chunk = rows[i: i + upload_batch_size]
            chunk_number = i // upload_batch_size + 1
            for attempt in range(1, _MAX_INSERT_ATTEMPTS + 1):
                try:
                    with conn.cursor() as cur:
                        cur.executemany(insert_sql, chunk)
                    conn.commit()
                    break
                except psycopg.Error as exc:
                    conn.close()
                    if attempt == _MAX_INSERT_ATTEMPTS:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            f"File {file_index}/{len(batch_files)} chunk {chunk_number} failed after {attempt} attempts."
                        ) from exc
                    logger.warning(
                        "File %d/%d chunk %d attempt %d failed (%s), reconnecting...",
                        file_index,
                        len(batch_files),
                        chunk_number,
                        attempt,
                        exc,
                    )
                    conn = _pg_connect()

        logger.info("Loaded attribute file %d/%d: %s", file_index, len(batch_files), batch_file.name)

    logger.info("Inserted %d rows into %s.snomed_attribute.", total_rows, schema)
    return conn

def load_attributes_from_db(snomed_relationships: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load SNOMED attribute value rows from the OHDSI Vocabularies DB."""
    engine = create_engine(get_environment_variable("VOCAB_CONNECTION_STRING"))
    schema = get_environment_variable("VOCAB_SCHEMA")
    rel_list = ", ".join(f"'{r}'" for r in snomed_relationships)
    df = pd.read_sql(f"""
        SELECT DISTINCT c2.concept_id, 
            c2.concept_code, 
            c2.concept_name,
            relationship_id AS attribute_category
        FROM {schema}.concept c
        INNER JOIN {schema}.concept_relationship cr
            ON  c.concept_id   = cr.concept_id_1
        INNER JOIN {schema}.concept c2 ON c2.concept_id = cr.concept_id_2
        WHERE c.vocabulary_id = 'SNOMED'
            AND c.standard_concept = 'S'
            AND cr.relationship_id IN ({rel_list})
            AND cr.invalid_reason IS NULL
            AND c2.invalid_reason IS NULL;
    """, engine)
    logger.info("Loaded %d attribute rows from DB.", len(df))
    return df

def classify_delta(
    delta_zip: str | Path,
    base_snomed_zip: str | None = None,
    *,
    toolkit_jar: str | None = None,
    java_xms: str = "4g",
    timeout: int = 600,
    output_dir: str | Path | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Run ELK classification via snomed-owl-toolkit.

    This calls the snomed-owl-toolkit's ``-classify`` command which:

    1. Converts the base SNOMED RF2 snapshot + your delta to OWL
    2. Runs the ELK reasoner to infer *Is a* relationships
    3. Produces a ``classification-results-*.zip`` with the inferred
       relationship changes

    Args:
        delta_zip: Path to the RF2 delta ZIP (from ``export_to_rf2``).
        base_snomed_zip: Path to the SNOMED CT International Edition RF2
            snapshot ZIP.  Falls back to ``SNOMED_BASE_RELEASE_ZIP`` env var.
        toolkit_jar: Path to the snomed-owl-toolkit executable JAR.
            Falls back to ``SNOMED_OWL_TOOLKIT_JAR`` env var, then
            ``tools/snomed-owl-toolkit.jar``.
        java_xms: JVM initial heap size (default ``4g``).
        timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for classification (default 600).
        output_dir: Directory where the results ZIP will be written.
            Defaults to the parent directory of *delta_zip*.

    Returns:
        Path to the classification results ZIP.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the classification process fails.
        FileNotFoundError: If the toolkit JAR or base release cannot be found.
        subprocess.TimeoutExpired: If classification exceeds *timeout*.
    """
    jar = _toolkit_jar(toolkit_jar)
    base = _base_release(base_snomed_zip)
    delta_zip = Path(delta_zip)
    output_dir = Path(output_dir or delta_zip.parent)

    cmd = [
        "java",
        f"-Xms{java_xms}",
        "--add-opens", "java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED",
        "-jar", jar,
        "-classify",
        "-rf2-snapshot-archives", base,
        "-rf2-authoring-delta-archive", str(delta_zip),
    ]

    logger.info("Running classification: %s", " ".join(cmd))
    result = subprocess.run(
        cmd,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=timeout,
        cwd=str(output_dir),
    )

    if result.stdout:
        logger.info("snomed-owl-toolkit stdout:\n%s", result.stdout)
    if result.stderr:
        logger.warning("snomed-owl-toolkit stderr:\n%s", result.stderr)

    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Classification failed (exit code {result.returncode}).\n"
            f"stderr:\n{result.stderr}\nstdout:\n{result.stdout}"
        )

    # Find the newest results ZIP
    pattern = str(output_dir / "classification-results-*.zip")
    candidates = sorted(glob.glob(pattern), key=os.path.getmtime)
    if not candidates:
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"No classification-results-*.zip found in {output_dir} after "
            "successful classification.  Check snomed-owl-toolkit output above."
        )

    results_zip = Path(candidates[-1])
    logger.info("Classification complete → %s", results_zip)
    return results_zip

def parse_classification_results(
    results_zip: str | Path,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Parse the classification results ZIP into DataFrames.

    Args:
        results_zip: Path to the ``classification-results-*.zip`` produced by
            :func:`classify_delta`.

    Returns:
        ``(new_is_a, removed_redundant, equiv_df)`` where:

        - **new_is_a** — DataFrame of newly inferred *Is a* relationships
          (``active == 1``, ``typeId == 116680003``).  Columns:
          ``sourceId``, ``destinationId``, plus all original RF2 columns.
        - **removed_redundant** — DataFrame of relationships marked inactive
          (``active == 0``).  These are stated relationships that became
          redundant after classification.
        - **equiv_df** — DataFrame of equivalent concept pairs from the
          EquivalentConceptSimpleMap refset.  Columns include
          ``referencedComponentId`` and ``mapTarget`` (group UUID).
    """
    results_zip = Path(results_zip)
    rel_dfs: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    equiv_df = pd.DataFrame()

    with zipfile.ZipFile(results_zip, "r") as zf:
        for name in zf.namelist():
            if "Relationship" in name and name.endswith(".txt"):
                with zf.open(name) as f:
                    df = pd.read_csv(f, sep="\t", dtype=str)
                    rel_dfs.append(df)

            # Parse equivalent concepts refset
            if "equivalent" in name.lower() or "equiv" in name.lower():
                with zf.open(name) as f:
                    equiv_df = pd.read_csv(f, sep="\t", dtype=str)
                    if len(equiv_df) > 0:
                        logger.warning(
                            "EQUIVALENT CONCEPTS FOUND (%d rows)!  "
                            "This usually indicates a modelling error — "
                            "two concepts have identical defining attributes.",
                            len(equiv_df),
                        )

    if not rel_dfs:
        logger.warning("No Relationship files found in %s", results_zip)
        empty = pd.DataFrame(columns=[
            "id", "effectiveTime", "active", "moduleId", "sourceId",
            "destinationId", "relationshipGroup", "typeId",
            "characteristicTypeId", "modifierId",
        ])
        return empty, empty, equiv_df

    all_rels = pd.concat(rel_dfs, ignore_index=True)

    new_is_a = all_rels[
        (all_rels["typeId"] == IS_A_TYPE_ID) & (all_rels["active"] == "1")
    ].copy()

    removed = all_rels[all_rels["active"] == "0"].copy()

    logger.info(
        "Classification results: %d new 'Is a' relationships, "
        "%d redundant removals, %d equivalent concept rows.",
        len(new_is_a), len(removed), len(equiv_df),
    )

    return new_is_a, removed, equiv_df

def pre_classification_checks(delta_zip: str | Path, hierarchy_settings: HierarchySettings) -> list[str]:
    """Run lightweight structural checks on an RF2 delta ZIP.

    Validates:
    - The ZIP contains the expected Terminology files
    - StatedRelationship file has correct TSV headers
    - All ``destinationId`` values look like valid SCTIDs (6+ digit integers)
    - All ``typeId`` values are "Is a" or an attribute configured in ``hierarchy.attributes``

    Args:
        delta_zip: Path to the RF2 delta ZIP.
        hierarchy_settings: ``config.hierarchy`` (source of the valid attribute type IDs).

    Returns:
        List of issue descriptions.  Empty list means all checks passed.
    """
    issues: list[str] = []
    delta_zip = Path(delta_zip)
    valid_type_ids = {IS_A_TYPE_ID, *(str(v) for v in hierarchy_settings.relationship_type_ids().values())}

    if not delta_zip.is_file():
        issues.append(f"Delta ZIP not found: {delta_zip}")
        return issues

    stated_found = False
    stated_row_count = 0
    owl_axiom_found = False
    owl_axiom_row_count = 0
    concept_found = False

    with zipfile.ZipFile(delta_zip, "r") as zf:
        for name in zf.namelist():
            if "StatedRelationship" in name and name.endswith(".txt"):
                stated_found = True
                with zf.open(name) as f:
                    df = pd.read_csv(f, sep="\t", dtype=str)

                stated_row_count = len(df)

                # Only validate content if file is non-empty
                if stated_row_count > 0:
                    expected_cols = {
                        "id", "effectiveTime", "active", "moduleId",
                        "sourceId", "destinationId", "relationshipGroup",
                        "typeId", "characteristicTypeId", "modifierId",
                    }
                    missing_cols = expected_cols - set(df.columns)
                    if missing_cols:
                        issues.append(f"StatedRelationship missing columns: {missing_cols}")

                    if "destinationId" in df.columns:
                        bad_dests = df[
                            ~df["destinationId"].str.match(r"^\d{6,18}$", na=False)
                        ]
                        if len(bad_dests) > 0:
                            samples = bad_dests["destinationId"].head(5).tolist()
                            issues.append(
                                f"{len(bad_dests)} destinationId values look invalid "
                                f"(expected 6-18 digit SCTIDs). Samples: {samples}"
                            )

                    if "typeId" in df.columns:
                        unknown_types = set(df["typeId"]) - valid_type_ids
                        if unknown_types:
                            issues.append(
                                f"Unknown typeId values (not 'Is a' or a configured attribute): "
                                f"{unknown_types}"
                            )

            elif "OWLAxiom" in name and name.endswith(".txt"):
                owl_axiom_found = True
                with zf.open(name) as f:
                    owl_df = pd.read_csv(f, sep="\t", dtype=str)

                # Filter to active rows only
                active_owl = owl_df[owl_df.get("active", pd.Series(dtype=str)) == "1"] if "active" in owl_df.columns else owl_df
                owl_axiom_row_count = len(active_owl)

                if owl_axiom_row_count > 0:
                    expected_owl_cols = {
                        "id", "active", "moduleId", "refsetId",
                        "referencedComponentId", "owlExpression",
                    }
                    missing_owl_cols = expected_owl_cols - set(owl_df.columns)
                    if missing_owl_cols:
                        issues.append(f"OWL Axiom refset missing columns: {missing_owl_cols}")
                    elif "owlExpression" in owl_df.columns:
                        # Validate each active expression starts with a known axiom type
                        bad_exprs = active_owl[
                            ~active_owl["owlExpression"].str.match(
                                r"^(EquivalentClasses|SubClassOf|TransitiveObjectProperty|ReflexiveObjectProperty)\(",
                                na=False,
                            )
                        ]
                        if len(bad_exprs) > 0:
                            samples = bad_exprs["owlExpression"].head(3).str[:80].tolist()
                            issues.append(
                                f"{len(bad_exprs)} OWL expressions do not start with a known "
                                f"axiom type (EquivalentClasses/SubClassOf/...). "
                                f"Samples: {samples}"
                            )

                        # Validate referencedComponentId looks like SCTIDs
                        if "referencedComponentId" in owl_df.columns:
                            bad_ids = active_owl[
                                ~active_owl["referencedComponentId"].str.match(
                                    r"^\d{6,18}$", na=False
                                )
                            ]
                            if len(bad_ids) > 0:
                                samples = bad_ids["referencedComponentId"].head(5).tolist()
                                issues.append(
                                    f"{len(bad_ids)} OWL axiom referencedComponentId values "
                                    f"look invalid. Samples: {samples}"
                                )

            if "Concept" in name and name.endswith(".txt") and "OWLAxiom" not in name:
                concept_found = True

    if not stated_found and not owl_axiom_found:
        issues.append(
            "No StatedRelationship or OWL Axiom refset file found in the delta ZIP."
        )
    elif stated_row_count == 0 and owl_axiom_row_count == 0:
        issues.append(
            "No concept definitions found: StatedRelationship is empty and OWL Axiom "
            "refset has no active rows.  At least one must contain data."
        )
    if not concept_found:
        issues.append("No Concept file found in the delta ZIP.")

    return issues

def drop_non_candidate_values(result: dict, candidates: pd.DataFrame | list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Remove selected concepts that were not offered as candidates for their attribute (in place).

    The selection prompt only allows candidates, but the LLM can copy a concept from the reference
    examples instead. Such values are removed from ``attributes``, ``llm_role_groups`` and
    ``role_groups``, and recorded in ``result["dropped_selections"]``.

    Args:
        result: Pipeline result with the selected concepts.
        candidates: The retrieved candidates (``candidates_df`` or ``result["retrieved_candidates"]``).

    Returns:
        The dropped values as ``{"attribute", "concept_id", "concept_name"}`` dicts.
    """
    rows = candidates.to_dict("records") if isinstance(candidates, pd.DataFrame) else list(candidates or [])
    allowed: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        allowed.setdefault(str(row.get("attribute_key")), set()).add(str(row.get("concept_id")))

    dropped: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}

    def keep(key: str, concept) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(concept, dict) or concept.get("concept_id") in (None, ""):
            return True
        concept_id = str(concept["concept_id"])
        if concept_id in allowed.get(EXTRACTION_KEY_ALIASES.get(key, key), set()):
            return True
        entry = dropped.setdefault(
            (key, concept_id), {"attribute": key, "concept_id": concept_id, "concept_name": None}
        )
        entry["concept_name"] = entry["concept_name"] or concept.get("concept_name")
        return False

    attributes = result.get("attributes")
    if isinstance(attributes, dict):
        for key, value in list(attributes.items()):
            if value is None:
                continue
            if key == INTERPRETS_PAIR_KEY and isinstance(value, list):
                attributes[key] = [
                    pair for pair in value
                    if not isinstance(pair, dict) or all([keep(k, v) for k, v in pair.items()])
                ]
            elif isinstance(value, list):
                attributes[key] = [concept for concept in value if keep(key, concept)]
            elif not keep(key, value):
                attributes[key] = None

    if "llm_role_groups" in result:
        groups = []
        for group in result.get("llm_role_groups") or []:
            if not isinstance(group, dict):
                groups.append(group)
                continue
            kept = {}
            for key, value in group.items():
                if isinstance(value, list):
                    kept[key] = [concept for concept in value if keep(key, concept)]
                elif keep(key, value):
                    kept[key] = value
            if any(kept.values()):
                groups.append(kept)
        if groups:
            result["llm_role_groups"] = groups
        else:
            result.pop("llm_role_groups")

    if "role_groups" in result:
        role_groups = []
        for group in result.get("role_groups") or []:
            members = [m for m in group.get("members", []) if keep(str(m.get("attribute")), m)]
            if members:
                role_groups.append({**group, "members": members})
        result["role_groups"] = role_groups

    if dropped:
        result["dropped_selections"] = result.get("dropped_selections", []) + list(dropped.values())
    return list(dropped.values())

def extract_attributes(
    source_term: str,
    attribute_searcher: AttributeSearcher,
    reference_searcher: ReferenceSearcher,
    hierarchy_settings: HierarchySettings | None = None
) -> dict:
    """Run the 4-step SNOMED CT attribute extraction pipeline.

    Steps:
        1. Retrieve reference examples (similar SNOMED concepts and their attributes).
        2. LLM infers applicable attributes.
        3. Retrieve SNOMED candidate values per attribute.
        4. LLM selects exact SNOMED concepts from candidates.

    Args:
        source_term: The clinical term to decompose.
        attribute_searcher: ``SnomedAttributeSearcher`` over the ``snomed_attribute`` table.
        reference_searcher: ``SnomedReferenceConceptVectorSearcher`` supplying few-shot
            reference examples.
        hierarchy_settings: Pipeline configuration.

    Returns:
        Dict with keys ``attributes``, ``role_groups``, ``grouping_method``,
        ``extracted_components``, ``retrieved_candidates``, ``reference_examples``,
        ``cost`` (plus ``llm_role_groups``/``mrcm_domain`` when available).
    """

    # Step 1
    logger.debug("Step 1: Finding reference examples")
    reference_examples, ref_cost = reference_searcher.search(source_term,
                                                             top_k=hierarchy_settings.retrieval.num_reference_examples)

    # Step 2
    logger.debug("Step 2: Inferring attributes")
    components, extraction_cost = infer_attributes(source_term,
                                                   reference_examples=reference_examples,
                                                   hierarchy_settings=hierarchy_settings)

    # Step 3
    logger.debug("Step 3: Retrieving candidates...")
    candidates_df, embedding_cost = _retrieve_candidates(
        components, attribute_searcher,
        hierarchy_settings=hierarchy_settings
    )

    # Step 4
    logger.debug("Step 4: Selecting best matches")
    candidates_text = _build_selection_prompt(candidates_df)
    selection_cost = 0.0
    if candidates_text.strip():
        reference_text = format_reference_examples(reference_examples, hierarchy_settings, include_concept_ids=True)
        system_prompt = _fill_prompt(hierarchy_settings.prompts.selection, reference_text, hierarchy_settings)
        user_prompt = f"Medical term: {source_term}\n\nCandidate concepts:\n{candidates_text}"
        extracted_groups_text = _format_extracted_role_groups(components)
        if extracted_groups_text:
            user_prompt += f"\n\n{extracted_groups_text}"
        response, selection_cost = call_llm(system_prompt, user_prompt)
        result = parse_json_response(response)
    else:
        logger.debug("Step 4 skipped: no candidates available for selection.")
        result = {"attributes": {}}

    total_cost = ref_cost + extraction_cost + embedding_cost + selection_cost

    llm_role_groups = _merge_role_groups_into_attributes(result)
    if llm_role_groups:
        result["llm_role_groups"] = llm_role_groups

    dropped = drop_non_candidate_values(result, candidates_df)
    if dropped:
        logger.warning(
            "%s: dropped selected value(s) not among the candidates: %s",
            source_term,
            "; ".join(f"{d['attribute']}={d['concept_name']} ({d['concept_id']})" for d in dropped),
        )

    # --- Enforce interprets ↔ interpretation pairing ---
    if "attributes" in result:
        _enforce_interprets_pairing(result["attributes"])

    _inject_selected_concept_codes(result, candidates_df)

    assign_role_groups(result, hierarchy_settings)
    _attach_pipeline_metadata(
        result,
        extracted_components=components,
        candidates_df=candidates_df,
        reference_examples=reference_examples,
        extraction_cost=extraction_cost,
        embedding_cost=embedding_cost,
        selection_cost=selection_cost,
        total_cost=total_cost,
    )
    logger.debug("Total cost: $%.4f", total_cost)
    return result

def format_reference_examples(
    similar_terms: list[dict], hierarchy_settings: HierarchySettings, include_concept_ids=False
) -> str:
    """Format reference examples into a human-readable block for the prompt.

    Args:
        similar_terms: List of reference dicts from the reference searcher.
        hierarchy_settings: Pipeline configuration; ``hierarchy.attributes`` names each relationship
            by its pipeline attribute key (e.g. ``"Has pathology"`` → ``pathological_process``).
            Relationships it doesn't list are shown by their OHDSI name.
        include_concept_ids: Append concept IDs to terms and attribute values.

    Returns:
        Formatted string, or empty string if no terms.
    """
    if not similar_terms:
        return ""
    attribute_key = hierarchy_settings.attribute_by_relationship()
    examples = []
    for term in similar_terms:
        attrs_text = []
        for a in term["attributes"]:
            line = f"  - {attribute_key.get(a['attribute_category'], a['attribute_category'])}: {a['target_concept_name']}"
            attrs_text.append(f"{line} ({a['target_concept_id']})" if include_concept_ids else line)
        attrs_str = "\n".join(attrs_text) if attrs_text else "  (no attributes)"
        if include_concept_ids:
            examples.append(f"Term: {term['concept_name']} ({term['concept_id']})\nAttributes:\n{attrs_str}")
        else:
            examples.append(f"Term: {term['concept_name']}\nAttributes:\n{attrs_str}")
    if not examples:
        return ""
    else:
        return "=== SIMILAR EXAMPLES ===\n" + "\n\n".join(examples)

def parse_json_response(response: str) -> dict:
    """Parse a JSON response from an LLM, stripping markdown fences if present.

    Args:
        response: Raw LLM response string.

    Returns:
        Parsed dict.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the response cannot be parsed as JSON.
    """
    raw = response  # keep original for diagnostics
    response = response.strip()
    if response.startswith("```"):
        response = response.split("```")[1]
        if response.startswith("json"):
            response = response[4:]
    try:
        return json.loads(response)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        logger.error(
            "Failed to parse LLM response as JSON. Raw response:\n%s", raw
        )
        raise ValueError(
            f"LLM returned malformed JSON: {exc}. "
            f"First 200 chars of response: {raw[:200]!r}"
        ) from exc

docs.title: llm_attribute_runner
docs.text:
Batch execution helpers for hierarchy attribute extraction.

The module exposes a single public entry point, :func:process_hierarchy, which executes the term-level extraction pipeline over a tabular dataset. Execution is resumable: each term's result is written to its own JSON file as soon as it succeeds, so an interrupted run resumes by reprocessing only the terms without a cached file. Failed terms are left uncached and retried on the next run.

Terms are processed concurrently by max_workers threads (the work is dominated by waiting on LLM API calls). Workers only run the extraction; caching, cost tracking and logging happen in the calling thread.

Load pipeline results from a JSON list file or a folder of per-term JSON files.

Unreadable per-term files and results without a source_key are skipped with a warning.

Source code in src/ariadne/hierarchy/llm_attribute_runner.py 
def load_hierarchy_results(path: str | Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Load pipeline results from a JSON list file or a folder of per-term JSON files.

    Unreadable per-term files and results without a ``source_key`` are skipped with a warning.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if path.is_file():
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        loaded = data if isinstance(data, list) else [data]
    else:
        loaded = []
        for file in sorted(path.glob("*.json")):
            try:
                with open(file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    loaded.append(json.load(f))
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
                logger.warning("Skipping unreadable result file %s: %s", file, exc)
    results = [r for r in loaded if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("source_key")]
    if len(results) < len(loaded):
        logger.warning("Skipped %d result(s) without a source_key in %s", len(loaded) - len(results), path)
    return results

def process_hierarchy(
    terms: pd.DataFrame,
    attribute_searcher: AttributeSearcher,
    reference_searcher: ReferenceSearcher,
    hierarchy_settings: HierarchySettings | None,
    source_term_column: str = "source_term",
    source_code_column: str = "source_concept_code",
    source_vocab_column: str = "source_vocabulary_id",
    source_id_column: str | None = "source_concept_id",
    checkpoint_every: int = 5,
    max_workers: int | None = None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """Execute hierarchy extraction over source terms with checkpoint resume.

    Parameters
    ----------
    terms
        Input rows containing source identifiers and term text.
    attribute_searcher
        Searcher used by the extraction pipeline for attribute candidates.
    reference_searcher
        Searcher used for optional reference concept lookups.
    hierarchy_settings
        Required runtime settings. ``evaluation.llm_response_folder`` is used to
        store one result file per source term for resume.
    source_term_column
        Name of the column containing source term text.
    source_code_column
        Name of the column containing the source concept code.
    source_vocab_column
        Name of the column containing the source vocabulary id. Combined with
        ``source_code_column`` to form the composite primary key.
    source_id_column
        Optional column with the OMOP ``concept_id`` (may be absent for new
        vocabularies). Carried through when present.
    checkpoint_every
        Cadence (in terms) for emitting a progress log line. Results are
        persisted immediately per term regardless of this value.
    max_workers
        Number of terms processed concurrently. Defaults to
        ``hierarchy_settings.evaluation.max_workers``; ``1`` runs sequentially.

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict]
        One result dictionary per processed source code: previously cached
        results first, then newly processed terms in input order.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``hierarchy_settings`` is missing.
    """
    if not hierarchy_settings:
        raise ValueError("HierarchySettings must be provided")

    results_dir = Path(hierarchy_settings.evaluation.llm_response_folder)

    all_results = load_hierarchy_results(results_dir)
    processed_ids = {r["source_key"] for r in all_results}
    if all_results:
        logger.info(
            "Resuming: %d terms already cached in %s", len(all_results), results_dir
        )
        _drop_cached_non_candidate_values(all_results, hierarchy_settings)

    has_source_id = bool(source_id_column) and source_id_column in terms.columns

    def _row_source_key(row) -> str:
        return _make_source_key(
            getattr(row, source_vocab_column), getattr(row, source_code_column)
        )

    pending_terms = [
        row for row in terms.itertuples(index=False) if _row_source_key(row) not in processed_ids
    ]

    if not pending_terms:
        logger.info("All terms already processed.")
        return all_results

    total_cost = sum(r.get("cost", {}).get("total_cost", 0.0) for r in all_results)
    if max_workers is None:
        max_workers = getattr(hierarchy_settings.evaluation, "max_workers", 1)

    def _source_meta(row) -> dict:
        source_concept_code = str(getattr(row, source_code_column))
        source_vocabulary_id = str(getattr(row, source_vocab_column))
        raw_id = getattr(row, source_id_column) if has_source_id else None
        return {
            "source_key": _make_source_key(source_vocabulary_id, source_concept_code),
            "source_concept_id": None if raw_id is None or pd.isna(raw_id) else raw_id,
            "source_concept_code": source_concept_code,
            "source_vocabulary_id": source_vocabulary_id,
            "source_term": str(getattr(row, source_term_column)),
        }

    def _worker(source_meta: dict) -> dict:
        logger.debug("\n%s\n%s", "=" * 60, source_meta["source_term"])
        return _process_term(
            source_meta,
            source_meta["source_term"],
            attribute_searcher,
            reference_searcher,
            hierarchy_settings,
        )

    pending_meta = [_source_meta(row) for row in pending_terms]
    new_results: list[dict | None] = [None] * len(pending_meta)
    logger.info(
        "Processing %d pending terms with %d worker(s)", len(pending_meta), max(1, max_workers)
    )

    for idx, result in run_concurrently(pending_meta, _worker, max_workers):
        new_results[idx] = result
        source_key = result["source_key"]

        # Do not cache failures: leaving them unpersisted means they are retried
        # on the next run (mirrors the LlmMapper per-response file cache).
        if "error" in result:
            logger.warning(
                "Term %s failed; not caching so it retries next run.", source_key
            )
            continue

        _save_result(results_dir, result)
        processed_ids.add(source_key)
        if "cost" in result:
            total_cost += result["cost"]["total_cost"]
            logger.debug(
                "  %s cost: $%.4f | running total: $%.4f",
                source_key,
                result["cost"]["total_cost"],
                total_cost,
            )

        if checkpoint_every > 0 and len(processed_ids) % checkpoint_every == 0:
            logger.info(
                "Processed %d/%d codes | Total API cost: $%.4f",
                len(processed_ids),
                len(terms),
                total_cost,
            )

    all_results.extend(r for r in new_results if r is not None)

    logger.debug(
        "\n%s\nCompleted: %d terms, Total cost: $%.4f",
        "=" * 60,
        len(all_results),
        total_cost,
    )

    return all_results

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Cardinality:
    """MRCM cardinality such as ``0..*`` or ``1..1``. ``max is None`` means unbounded."""

    min: int
    max: int | None

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> "Cardinality":
        low, _, high = text.strip().partition("..")
        return cls(int(low), None if high in ("*", "") else int(high))

    def allows(self, count: int) -> bool:
        return count >= self.min and (self.max is None or count <= self.max)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.min}..{'*' if self.max is None else self.max}"

@dataclass
class MrcmRules:
    """MRCM rules for the configured domains, addressable by pipeline attribute key."""

    settings: MrcmSettings
    domains: dict[str, MrcmDomain]
    attribute_rules: dict[int, dict[int, AttributeRule]]
    range_rules: dict[int, list[RangeRule]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # ``hierarchy.attributes``: pipeline attribute key -> SNOMED attribute concept.
    attributes: dict[str, AttributeConfig] = field(default_factory=dict)

    # ── construction ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, settings: MrcmSettings, attributes: Mapping[str, AttributeConfig]) -> "MrcmRules":
        """Load MRCM rules from the RF2 refset files in ``settings.folder``.

        Args:
            settings: ``hierarchy.mrcm``.
            attributes: ``hierarchy.attributes``; maps pipeline attribute keys to MRCM attribute IDs.
        """
        folder = Path(settings.folder)
        content_types = {int(c) for c in settings.content_types}
        wanted = {int(d): name for name, d in settings.domains.items()}

        domains: dict[str, MrcmDomain] = {}
        for row in _read_active_rows(folder, _DOMAIN_GLOB):
            domain_id = int(row["referencedComponentId"])
            if domain_id in wanted:
                domains[wanted[domain_id]] = MrcmDomain(
                    name=wanted[domain_id],
                    domain_id=domain_id,
                    parent_domain_id=_leading_id(row.get("parentDomain", "")),
                )
        missing = set(wanted.values()) - set(domains)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"MRCM domains not found in {folder}: {sorted(missing)}")

        attribute_rules: dict[int, dict[int, AttributeRule]] = defaultdict(dict)
        for row in _read_active_rows(folder, _ATTRIBUTE_DOMAIN_GLOB):
            domain_id = int(row["domainId"])
            content_type = int(row["contentTypeId"])
            if domain_id not in wanted or content_type not in content_types:
                continue
            attribute_id = int(row["referencedComponentId"])
            attribute_rules[domain_id][attribute_id] = AttributeRule(
                attribute_id=attribute_id,
                domain_id=domain_id,
                grouped=row["grouped"] == "1",
                cardinality=Cardinality.parse(row["attributeCardinality"]),
                in_group_cardinality=Cardinality.parse(row["attributeInGroupCardinality"]),
            )

        relevant_attributes = {a for rules in attribute_rules.values() for a in rules}
        range_rules: dict[int, list[RangeRule]] = defaultdict(list)
        for row in _read_active_rows(folder, _ATTRIBUTE_RANGE_GLOB):
            attribute_id = int(row["referencedComponentId"])
            content_type = int(row["contentTypeId"])
            if attribute_id not in relevant_attributes or content_type not in content_types:
                continue
            range_rules[attribute_id].append(
                RangeRule(
                    attribute_id=attribute_id,
                    range_constraint=row["rangeConstraint"],
                    focus=parse_simple_ecl(row["rangeConstraint"]),
                )
            )

        return cls(settings, domains, dict(attribute_rules), dict(range_rules), dict(attributes))

    # ── attribute key helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def attribute_id(self, attribute_key: str) -> int | None:
        config = self.attributes.get(attribute_key)
        return config.attribute_id if config else None

    def attribute_key(self, attribute_id: int) -> str | None:
        for key, config in self.attributes.items():
            if config.attribute_id == attribute_id:
                return key
        return None

    # ── domain helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def domain_chain(self, domain_name: str) -> list[MrcmDomain]:
        """The domain followed by its configured MRCM ancestors (nearest first)."""
        by_id = {d.domain_id: d for d in self.domains.values()}
        chain, current = [], self.domains[domain_name]
        while current is not None and current not in chain:
            chain.append(current)
            current = by_id.get(current.parent_domain_id) if current.parent_domain_id else None
        return chain

    def rules_for_domain(self, domain_name: str) -> dict[str, AttributeRule]:
        """Attribute rules (own + inherited) of a domain keyed by pipeline attribute key.

        Attributes allowed by the MRCM but without a pipeline key are keyed ``"<id>"``.
        """
        rules: dict[int, AttributeRule] = {}
        for domain in reversed(self.domain_chain(domain_name)):
            rules.update(self.attribute_rules.get(domain.domain_id, {}))
        return {(self.attribute_key(a) or str(a)): rule for a, rule in rules.items()}

    def select_domain(self, attribute_keys: Iterable[str]) -> str:
        """Pick the configured domain that allows the most of ``attribute_keys``.

        Ties go to ``default_domain`` and then to the most specific (deepest) domain.
        """
        keys = set(attribute_keys)
        default = self.settings.default_domain or next(iter(self.domains))

        def score(name: str) -> tuple[int, bool, int]:
            allowed = set(self.rules_for_domain(name))
            return len(keys & allowed), name == default, len(self.domain_chain(name))

        return max(self.domains, key=score)

    def ranges(self, attribute_key: str) -> list[RangeRule]:
        attribute_id = self.attribute_id(attribute_key)
        return self.range_rules.get(attribute_id, []) if attribute_id is not None else []

    def in_range(self, attribute_key: str, concept_code: str, is_a: IsAFunction) -> bool | None:
        """Whether ``concept_code`` satisfies any range rule of the attribute.

        Returns ``None`` when no range rule could be evaluated (unsupported ECL).
        """
        evaluable = [r for r in self.ranges(attribute_key) if r.focus is not None]
        if not evaluable:
            return None
        code = str(concept_code)
        for rule in evaluable:
            for operator, focus in rule.focus or ():
                if operator == "" and code == focus:
                    return True
                if operator == "<<" and is_a(code, focus):
                    return True
                if operator == "<" and code != focus and is_a(code, focus):
                    return True
        return False

class Rf2IsAIndex:
    """Transitive ``is a`` lookups built from an RF2 relationship snapshot (inferred, active)."""

    def __init__(self, parents: dict[str, set[str]]):
        self._parents = parents
        self._ancestors: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {}

    @classmethod
    def from_relationship_file(cls, path: str | Path) -> "Rf2IsAIndex":
        parents: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            next(handle)
            for line in handle:
                cols = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
                if cols[2] == "1" and cols[7] == IS_A_TYPE_ID and cols[8] == INFERRED_CHARACTERISTIC_TYPE_ID:
                    parents[cols[4]].add(cols[5])
        return cls(dict(parents))

    def ancestors(self, concept_code: str) -> frozenset[str]:
        cached = self._ancestors.get(concept_code)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        seen: set[str] = set()
        stack = list(self._parents.get(concept_code, ()))
        while stack:
            parent = stack.pop()
            if parent not in seen:
                seen.add(parent)
                stack.extend(self._parents.get(parent, ()))
        result = frozenset(seen)
        self._ancestors[concept_code] = result
        return result

    def __contains__(self, concept_code: object) -> bool:
        """True if the concept has an active inferred ``is a`` (i.e. is active, non-root)."""
        return str(concept_code) in self._parents

    def __call__(self, concept_code: str, ancestor_code: str) -> bool:
        concept_code, ancestor_code = str(concept_code), str(ancestor_code)
        return concept_code == ancestor_code or ancestor_code in self.ancestors(concept_code)

def build_grouping_prompt_section(settings: MrcmSettings) -> str:
    """Human-readable role-grouping rules injected into the hierarchy prompts."""
    grouping = settings.grouping
    if not grouping.enabled:
        return ""
    llm_keys = grouping.llm_grouped_keys()
    lines = ["# Role Groups (SNOMED CT concept model)"]
    if llm_keys:
        lines += [
            f"- {', '.join(llm_keys)} are reported inside \"role_groups\": a list of groups, "
            "each group describing ONE disease process (one site with its morphology/process/agent/occurrence).",
            "- Use ONE group when the term describes one process. Use SEVERAL groups only when the term names "
            "several distinct sites or lesions (e.g. 'X of A and B', 'fracture of radius and ulna').",
            "- Each group contains at most one value per attribute. Repeat a shared value (e.g. the same morphology) "
            "in every group it applies to.",
        ]
    if grouping.self_grouped:
        lines.append(
            f"- {', '.join(grouping.self_grouped)} are always reported at the top level, never inside role_groups."
        )
    other = [k for name, keys in grouping.clusters.items() if name not in grouping.llm_grouped_clusters for k in keys]
    if {"interprets", "interpretation"} & set(other):
        other = [k for k in other if k not in ("interprets", "interpretation")] + ["interprets_interpretation"]
    if other:
        lines.append(f"- {', '.join(other)} are reported at the top level, never inside role_groups.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def parse_simple_ecl(constraint: str) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] | None:
    """Parse an ECL disjunction of ``<<id``, ``<id`` or ``id`` terms.

    Returns ``None`` for anything more complex (refinements, MINUS, AND, nesting),
    in which case range checks are skipped for that rule.
    """
    text = _PIPE_TERM.sub("", constraint).strip()
    if not text or any(tok in text for tok in ("(", ")", ":", "{", "MINUS", " AND ")):
        return None
    parts = []
    for part in text.split(" OR "):
        match = _SIMPLE_FOCUS.match(part.strip())
        if not match:
            return None
        parts.append((match.group(1), match.group(2)))
    return tuple(parts)

def validate_result(result: dict, rules: MrcmRules, is_a: IsAFunction | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Validate one pipeline result. Results without ``role_groups`` are grouped first."""
    if not isinstance(result, dict) or result.get("error"):
        return []
    if result.get("role_groups") is None:
        result = regroup_result(result, rules.settings, rules)
    role_groups: list[dict] = result.get("role_groups") or []
    if not role_groups:
        return []

    grouping = rules.settings.grouping
    domain = result.get("mrcm_domain") or rules.select_domain(
        m.get("attribute") for g in role_groups for m in g.get("members", []))
    domain_rules = rules.rules_for_domain(domain)
    base = {"source_key": result.get("source_key"), "source_term": result.get("source_term"), "mrcm_domain": domain}
    violations: list[dict] = []

    def add(rule: str, severity: str, detail: str, attribute=None, group=None, member=None) -> None:
        violations.append({
            **base,
            "rule": rule,
            "severity": severity,
            "attribute": attribute,
            "group": group,
            "concept_id": member.get("concept_id") if member else None,
            "concept_name": member.get("concept_name") if member else None,
            "detail": detail,
        })

    # Attribute level: configured, allowed in domain, value in range.
    values_by_key: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    checked: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    for group in role_groups:
        number = group.get("group")
        for member in group.get("members", []):
            key = member.get("attribute")
            values_by_key.setdefault(key, set()).add(str(member.get("concept_id")))
            if (key, str(member.get("concept_id"))) in checked:
                continue
            checked.add((key, str(member.get("concept_id"))))
            if key not in rules.attributes:
                add("unknown_attribute", ERROR, f"'{key}' is not configured in hierarchy.attributes", key, number, member)
                continue
            if key not in domain_rules:
                add("attribute_not_in_domain", ERROR, f"MRCM does not allow '{key}' in domain '{domain}'", key, number, member)
                continue
            code = member.get("concept_code")
            if is_a is not None and code not in (None, ""):
                in_range = rules.in_range(key, str(code), is_a)
                if in_range is False:
                    constraints = " OR ".join(r.range_constraint for r in rules.ranges(key))
                    inactive = hasattr(is_a, "__contains__") and str(code) not in is_a  # type: ignore[operator]
                    reason = "is not active in the RF2 release" if inactive else f"is outside range: {constraints}"
                    add("attribute_range", ERROR, f"{code} {reason}", key, number, member)

    for key, concept_ids in values_by_key.items():
        rule = domain_rules.get(key)
        if rule is not None and not rule.cardinality.allows(len(concept_ids)):
            add("attribute_cardinality", ERROR,
                f"{len(concept_ids)} values; MRCM cardinality {rule.cardinality}", key)

    # Group level.
    signatures: Counter = Counter()
    for group in role_groups:
        number = group.get("group")
        members = group.get("members", [])
        keys = [m.get("attribute") for m in members]
        signatures[frozenset((m.get("attribute"), str(m.get("concept_id"))) for m in members)] += 1

        for key, count in Counter(keys).items():
            rule = domain_rules.get(key)
            if rule is None:
                continue
            if number != 0 and not rule.in_group_cardinality.allows(count):
                add("in_group_cardinality", ERROR,
                    f"{count} values in group {number}; MRCM in-group cardinality {rule.in_group_cardinality}",
                    key, number)
            if (number == 0) == rule.grouped:
                expected = "a role group" if rule.grouped else "group 0"
                add("grouped_mismatch", ERROR, f"'{key}' must be in {expected}", key, number)

        if number == 0:
            continue
        for key in set(keys) & set(grouping.self_grouped):
            if len(members) > 1:
                add("self_grouped_shared", ERROR,
                    f"'{key}' must be alone in its role group; group {number} has {sorted(set(keys))}", key, number)
        clusters = {grouping.cluster_of(k) for k in keys if grouping.cluster_of(k) and k not in grouping.self_grouped}
        if len(clusters) > 1:
            add("cluster_mix", ERROR, f"group {number} mixes clusters {sorted(clusters)}: {sorted(set(keys))}",
                group=number)
        for key, partner in grouping.requires.items():
            if key in keys and partner not in keys:
                add("missing_required_partner", ERROR, f"'{key}' requires '{partner}' in group {number}", key, number)

    duplicates = sum(count - 1 for count in signatures.values() if count > 1)
    if duplicates:
        add("duplicate_group", WARNING, f"{duplicates} duplicated role group(s)")
    if result.get("grouping_method") == METHOD_POSITIONAL:
        add("ambiguous_grouping", WARNING,
            "several attributes have several values; groups were paired by position and may be wrong")
    return violations

        rules: Loaded MRCM rules.
        is_a: Optional ``is_a(concept_code, ancestor_code)`` callable (e.g.
            :class:`~ariadne.hierarchy.mrcm.Rf2IsAIndex`) enabling MRCM range checks.
    """
    rows = [v for result in results for v in validate_result(result, rules, is_a)]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=VIOLATION_COLUMNS)

docs.title: parent_selector
docs.text:
Stated parent selection for new SNOMED CT clinical concepts.

The RF2 exporter writes new concepts as sufficiently defined, so the classifier can infer fully defined supertypes from the attributes but never primitive ones. The stated parent therefore has to be a primitive concept, ideally the proximal primitive parent.

Allowed parents are the primitive SNOMED descendants of root_concept_id (Clinical finding); the root itself is the fallback.

docs.title: Algorithm, per source term
docs.text:
1. Neighbours: the num_neighbours most similar standard SNOMED concepts (embedding search) with similarity >= min_similarity. With exclude_source_descendants the source concept and its descendants are dropped first, because they would not exist for a genuinely new concept.
  2. Candidates: the primitive ancestors of each neighbour (the neighbour itself excluded).
  3. Support: the similarity-weighted share of neighbours below each candidate.
  4. Selection: candidates with support >= min_support, minus any candidate that is an ancestor of another qualifying candidate, deepest first (min_levels_of_separation from the root), capped at max_parents. When neighbours agree this is their proximal primitive parent; when they disagree it is an intermediate primitive.
  5. Fallback: the root when no candidate qualifies.

Usage::

with psycopg.connect(conn_str) as conn:
    stated_parents, details = build_stated_parents_map(
        raw_results, conn, schema, config.hierarchy.parent_selection
    )
# stated_parents: {source_concept_id (or source_key): [parent_sctid, ...]}
